passages.claim: A federal estate tax return is required only above the filing threshold for the year of death: $15,000,000 for 2026 ($13,990,000 for 2025).
passages.quote: A filing is required if the gross estate of the decedent, increased by the decedent's adjusted taxable gifts and specific gift tax exemption, is valued at more than the filing threshold for the year of the decedent's death, as shown in the table below. ... 2025 | $13,990,000 ... 2026 | $15,000,000

passages.claim: The gross estate counts everything at fair market value, including real estate and trusts.
passages.quote: The fair market value of these items is used, not necessarily what you paid for them or what their values were when you acquired them. The total of all of these items is your "Gross Estate." The includible property may consist of cash and securities, real estate, insurance, trusts, annuities, business interests and other assets.

passages.claim: A surviving spouse can receive the first spouse's unused exclusion, but only by an election on a timely filed estate tax return.
passages.quote: Beginning January 1, 2011, estates of decedents survived by a spouse may elect to pass any of the decedent's unused exemption to the surviving spouse. This election is made on a timely filed estate tax return for the decedent with a surviving spouse.

title: IR-2026-133 (Nov. 5, 2026): tax inflation adjustments for tax year 2027 (announces Rev. Proc. 2026-35)

passages.claim: Basic exclusion amount: $15,480,000 for deaths in 2027, $15,000,000 for deaths in 2026.
passages.quote: Estates of decedents who die during 2027 have a basic exclusion amount of $15,480,000, up from a total of $15,000,000 for estates of decedents who died in 2026.

passages.claim: Annual gift exclusion: $20,000 per recipient in 2027, $19,000 in 2026.
passages.quote: For calendar year 2027, the annual exclusion for gifts increases to $20,000, up from $19,000 for calendar year 2026.

passages.claim: 2027 standard deduction: $33,200 joint, $16,600 single.
passages.quote: For tax year 2027, the standard deduction increases to $33,200 for married couples filing jointly, up $1,000 from 2026. For single taxpayers and married individuals filing separately, the standard deduction rises to $16,600 for tax year 2027

the top tax rate remains 37% for individual single taxpayers with incomes greater than $661,375 ($793,650 for married couples filing jointly). The other rates are: 35% for incomes over $264,550 ($529,100 for married couples filing jointly); 32% for incomes over $208,325 ($416,650 for married couples filing jointly); 24% for incomes over $109,125 ($218,250 for married couples filing jointly); 22% for incomes over $52,025 ($104,050 for married couples filing jointly); 12% for incomes over $12,800 ($25,600 for married couples filing jointly).

title: Frequently asked questions on estate taxes

passages.claim: To pass the unused exclusion to the surviving spouse (portability), Form 706 must be filed even when the estate is below the threshold.
passages.quote: An estate tax return also must be filed if the estate elects to transfer any deceased spousal unused exclusion (DSUE) amount to a surviving spouse, regardless of the size of the gross estate or amount of adjusted taxable gifts. The election to transfer a DSUE amount to a surviving spouse is known as the portability election.

passages.claim: Deadline for the portability return: nine months after death, with an automatic six-month extension on Form 4768.
passages.quote: The due date of the estate tax return is nine months after the decedent's date of death, however, the estate's representative may request an extension of time to file the return for up to six months. An automatic six month extension of time to file the return is available to all estates, including those filing solely to elect portability, by filing Form 4768 on or before the due date of the estate tax return.

passages.claim: If the deadline is missed and the estate is below the filing threshold, a late portability election is possible until the fifth anniversary of death under Rev. Proc. 2022-32.
passages.quote: The simplified method under the revenue procedure to obtain an extension of time to make the portability election requires the filing of a complete and properly prepared estate tax return on or before the fifth annual anniversary of the decedent's date of death

passages.claim: The $15,000,000 amount for 2026 comes from Public Law 119-21, signed July 4, 2025.
passages.quote: The Working Families Tax Cuts Bill was signed into law on July 4, 2025 as Public Law 119-21 and amends § 2010(c)(3) by increasing the basic exclusion amount to $15,000,000 for gifts for calendar year 2026.

title: Gifts & inheritances: Is money received from the sale of inherited property considered taxable income?

passages.claim: The income-tax basis of inherited property is generally its fair market value on the date of death (or on the alternate valuation date if elected on Form 706).
passages.quote: The basis of property inherited from a decedent is generally one of the following: The fair market value (FMV) of the property on the date of the decedent's death (whether or not the executor of the estate files an estate tax return ... The FMV of the property on the alternate valuation date, but only if the executor of the estate files an estate tax return (Form 706) and elects to use the alternate valuation on that return.

passages.claim: Only the amount above that basis is a taxable gain on sale.
passages.quote: If you sell the property for more than your basis, you have a taxable gain.

passages.claim: If an estate tax return is filed, the heir may have to use the estate-tax value as basis (Form 8971, Schedule A).
passages.quote: If you receive a Schedule A to Form 8971 from an executor of an estate or other person required to file an estate tax return, you may be required to report a basis consistent with the estate tax value of the property.

title: Topic no. 425, Passive activities - Losses and credits

passages.claim: A rental loss (for example one created by depreciation) generally cannot offset wages; it is carried forward.
passages.quote: Generally, passive activity losses that exceed the passive activity income are disallowed for the current year. You can carry forward disallowed passive losses to the next taxable year.

passages.claim: Rental real estate is generally a passive activity.
passages.quote: In general, rental activities, including rental real estate activities, are passive activities even if you materially participate.

passages.claim: Suspended losses are released when the property is sold.
passages.quote: Generally, you may fully deduct any previously disallowed passive activity loss in the year you dispose of your entire interest in the activity.

title: Proposition 19 (comparison chart, former law vs current law)

passages.claim: The parent-child exclusion now requires the home to be the principal residence of both the parent and the child, and is capped at the current taxable value plus $1,000,000 (adjusted every two years).
passages.quote: Principal residence of transferor and transferee ... Value limit of current taxable value plus $1,000,000 (as biennially adjusted) ... Family homes and farms

passages.claim: No exclusion remains for any other real property (a rental, a second home).
passages.quote: Eliminates exclusion for other real property other than the principal residence

passages.claim: Two filing deadlines: homeowners' exemption within one year; exclusion claim within three years or before a transfer to a third party.
passages.quote: File for homeowners' exemption within 1 year of transfer ... File claim for exclusion within 3 years or before transfer to third party

passages.claim: Operative for parent-child transfers since February 16, 2021; implemented by Revenue and Taxation Code section 63.2.
passages.quote: Proposition 19's provisions became operative on February 16, 2021 (for intergenerational transfer exclusions) ... Senate Bill 539 (Stats. 2021, ch. 427) added sections 63.2 and 69.6 to the Revenue and Taxation Code to implement the provisions of Proposition 19.
